My work applies modern causal-inference methods — synthetic control, regression
discontinuity, difference-in-differences — to questions in political economy,
development, and public policy.

```{=html}
<div class="section-label">Working papers</div>

<div class="paper-card" style="border-left:4px solid var(--clay);">
  <h3><a href="research/fences-and-fortunes/">Fences and Fortunes: The Effect of Enhanced Border Enforcement on El Paso</a></h3>
  <div class="meta">with Robin Grier and Kevin Grier · Under review</div>
  <p class="abstract">
    Using household-level difference-in-differences and county-level synthetic
    control, we estimate the effects of 1993's Operation Hold the Line on El
    Paso. Incomes, house values, population, and business establishments all
    fell relative to their counterfactuals; property and violent crime declined.
    A cost-benefit analysis finds the costs substantially outweighed the
    benefits.
  </p>
  <div class="paper-links">
    <a class="primary" href="research/fences-and-fortunes/">Data companion</a>

  <h3>Mobile Phones and Collective Violent Action: Evidence from the Libyan Revolution</h3>
  <div class="meta">with Kevin Grier · Working paper</div>
  <p class="abstract">
    Did mobile-phone coverage shape where collective violence broke out during
    the 2011 Libyan Revolution? We exploit the regime's own network blackouts to
    find out.
  </p>
  <div class="paper-links">
    <a href="mailto:sam.r.absher@gmail.com?subject=Libya%20draft">Draft on request</a>

  <h3>The Persistent Effects of Military Violence Against Civilians</h3>
  <div class="meta">Working paper</div>

    East Germany and its long-run consequences for the communities that
    experienced it.

  <h3>Willingness to Pay for School Quality: An Application of Spatial First Differences</h3>
  <div class="meta">with Jason Ward and Susha Roy · In progress</div>
  <p class="abstract">
    How much do home buyers pay for better schools? We estimate capitalization
    of school quality into Los Angeles house prices using spatial first
    differences.
```
